units.leftText: In the second year of Darius the king, in the sixth month, in the first day of the month, the LORD’s word came by Haggai the prophet, to Zerubbabel the son of Shealtiel, governor of Judah, and to Joshua the son of Jehozadak, the high priest, saying,
units.rightText: In the second year of the reign of Darius, on the first day of the sixth month, the word of the LORD came through Haggai the prophet to Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel, governor of Judah, and to Joshua son of Jehozadak, the high priest, stating
leftNotes: 1:1 When rendered in ALL CAPITAL LETTERS, “LORD” or “GOD” is the translation of God’s Proper Name (Hebrew “יהוה*”, usually pronounced Yahweh).
rightNotes: 1:1 Jehozadak is a variant of Jozadak; also in verses 12 and 14; see Ezra 3:2|EZR 3:2*.

units.leftText: “This is what the LORD of Armies says: These people say, ‘The time hasn’t yet come, the time for the LORD’s house to be built.’”
units.rightText: that this is what the LORD of Hosts says: “These people say, ‘The time has not yet come to rebuild the house of the LORD.’”

units.leftText: Then the LORD’s word came by Haggai the prophet, saying,
units.rightText: Then the word of the LORD came through Haggai the prophet, saying:

units.leftText: “Is it a time for you yourselves to dwell in your paneled houses, while this house lies waste?
units.rightText: “Is it a time for you yourselves to live in your paneled houses, while this house lies in ruins?”

units.leftText: Now therefore this is what the LORD of Armies says: ‘Consider your ways.
units.rightText: Now this is what the LORD of Hosts says: “Consider carefully your ways.

units.leftText: You have sown much, and bring in little. You eat, but you don’t have enough. You drink, but you aren’t filled with drink. You clothe yourselves, but no one is warm; and he who earns wages earns wages to put them into a bag with holes in it.’
units.rightText: You have planted much but harvested little. You eat but never have enough. You drink but never have your fill. You put on clothes but never get warm. You earn wages to put into a bag pierced through.”

units.leftText: “This is what the LORD of Armies says: ‘Consider your ways.
units.rightText: This is what the LORD of Hosts says: “Consider carefully your ways.

units.leftText: Go up to the mountain, bring wood, and build the house. I will take pleasure in it, and I will be glorified,” says the LORD.
units.rightText: Go up into the hills, bring down lumber, and build the house, so that I may take pleasure in it and be glorified, says the LORD.

units.leftText: “You looked for much, and, behold, it came to little; and when you brought it home, I blew it away. Why?” says the LORD of Armies, “Because of my house that lies waste, while each of you is busy with his own house.
units.rightText: You expected much, but behold, it amounted to little. And what you brought home, I blew away. Why? declares the LORD of Hosts. Because My house still lies in ruins, while each of you is busy with his own house.
leftNotes: 1:9 “Behold”, from “הִנֵּה*”, means look at, take notice, observe, see, or gaze at. It is often used as an interjection.

units.leftText: Therefore for your sake the heavens withhold the dew, and the earth withholds its fruit.
units.rightText: Therefore, on account of you the heavens have withheld their dew and the earth has withheld its crops.

units.leftText: I called for a drought on the land, on the mountains, on the grain, on the new wine, on the oil, on that which the ground produces, on men, on livestock, and on all the labor of the hands.”
units.rightText: I have summoned a drought on the fields and on the mountains, on the grain, new wine, and oil, and on whatever the ground yields, on man and beast, and on all the labor of your hands.” The People Obey

units.leftText: Then Zerubbabel the son of Shealtiel and Joshua the son of Jehozadak, the high priest, with all the remnant of the people, obeyed the LORD their God’s voice, and the words of Haggai the prophet, as the LORD their God had sent him; and the people feared the LORD.
units.rightText: Then Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel and Joshua son of Jehozadak, the high priest, as well as all the remnant of the people, obeyed the voice of the LORD their God and the words of the prophet Haggai, because the LORD their God had sent him. So the people feared the LORD.

units.leftText: Then Haggai, the LORD’s messenger, spoke the LORD’s message to the people, saying, “I am with you,” says the LORD.
units.rightText: Haggai, the messenger of the LORD, delivered the message of the LORD to the people: “I am with you,” declares the LORD.

units.leftText: The LORD stirred up the spirit of Zerubbabel the son of Shealtiel, governor of Judah, and the spirit of Joshua the son of Jehozadak, the high priest, and the spirit of all the remnant of the people; and they came and worked on the house of the LORD of Armies, their God,
units.rightText: So the LORD stirred the spirit of Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel, governor of Judah, and the spirit of Joshua son of Jehozadak, the high priest, as well as the spirit of all the remnant of the people. And they came and began the work on the house of the LORD of Hosts, their God,

units.leftText: in the twenty-fourth day of the month, in the sixth month, in the second year of Darius the king.
units.rightText: on the twenty-fourth day of the sixth month, in the second year of King Darius.

units.leftText: In the seventh month, in the twenty-first day of the month, the LORD’s word came by Haggai the prophet, saying,
units.rightText: On the twenty-first day of the seventh month, the word of the LORD came through Haggai the prophet, saying:

units.leftText: “Speak now to Zerubbabel the son of Shealtiel, governor of Judah, and to Joshua the son of Jehozadak, the high priest, and to the remnant of the people, saying,
units.rightText: “Speak to Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel, governor of Judah, and to Joshua son of Jehozadak, the high priest, and also to the remnant of the people. Ask them,
rightNotes: 2:2 Jehozadak is a variant of Jozadak; also in verse 4; see Ezra 3:2|EZR 3:2*.

units.leftText: ‘Who is left among you who saw this house in its former glory? How do you see it now? Isn’t it in your eyes as nothing?
units.rightText: ‘Who is left among you who saw this house in its former glory? How does it look to you now? Does it not appear to you like nothing in comparison?’

units.leftText: Yet now be strong, Zerubbabel,’ says the LORD. ‘Be strong, Joshua son of Jehozadak, the high priest. Be strong, all you people of the land,’ says the LORD, ‘and work, for I am with you,’ says the LORD of Armies.
units.rightText: But now be strong, O Zerubbabel, declares the LORD. Be strong, O Joshua son of Jehozadak, the high priest. And be strong, all you people of the land, declares the LORD. Work! For I am with you, declares the LORD of Hosts.

units.leftText: This is the word that I covenanted with you when you came out of Egypt, and my Spirit lived among you. ‘Don’t be afraid.’
units.rightText: This is the promise I made to you when you came out of Egypt. And My Spirit remains among you; do not be afraid.”

units.leftText: For this is what the LORD of Armies says: ‘Yet once more, it is a little while, and I will shake the heavens, the earth, the sea, and the dry land;
units.rightText: For this is what the LORD of Hosts says: “Once more, in a little while, I will shake the heavens and the earth, the sea and the dry land.

units.leftText: and I will shake all nations. The treasure of all nations will come, and I will fill this house with glory, says the LORD of Armies.
units.rightText: I will shake all the nations, and they will come with all their treasures, and I will fill this house with glory, says the LORD of Hosts.

units.leftText: The silver is mine, and the gold is mine,’ says the LORD of Armies.
units.rightText: The silver is Mine, and the gold is Mine, declares the LORD of Hosts.

units.leftText: ‘The latter glory of this house will be greater than the former,’ says the LORD of Armies; ‘and in this place I will give peace,’ says the LORD of Armies.”
units.rightText: The latter glory of this house will be greater than the former, says the LORD of Hosts. And in this place I will provide peace, declares the LORD of Hosts.” Blessings for a Defiled People

units.leftText: In the twenty-fourth day of the ninth month, in the second year of Darius, the LORD’s word came by Haggai the prophet, saying,
units.rightText: On the twenty-fourth day of the ninth month, in the second year of Darius, the word of the LORD came to Haggai the prophet, saying,

units.leftText: “The LORD of Armies says: Ask now the priests concerning the law, saying,
units.rightText: “This is what the LORD of Hosts says: ‘Ask the priests for a ruling.

units.leftText: ‘If someone carries holy meat in the fold of his garment, and with his fold touches bread, stew, wine, oil, or any food, will it become holy?’” The priests answered, “No.”
units.rightText: If a man carries consecrated meat in the fold of his garment, and it touches bread, stew, wine, oil, or any other food, does that item become holy?’” “No,” replied the priests.

units.leftText: Then Haggai said, “If one who is unclean by reason of a dead body touches any of these, will it be unclean?” The priests answered, “It will be unclean.”
units.rightText: So Haggai asked, “If one who is defiled by contact with a corpse touches any of these, does it become defiled?” “Yes, it becomes defiled,” the priests answered.

units.leftText: Then Haggai answered, “‘So is this people, and so is this nation before me,’ says the LORD; ‘and so is every work of their hands. That which they offer there is unclean.
units.rightText: Then Haggai replied, “So it is with this people and this nation before Me, declares the LORD, and so it is with every work of their hands; whatever they offer there is defiled.

units.leftText: Now, please consider from this day and backward, before a stone was laid on a stone in the LORD’s temple.
units.rightText: Now consider carefully from this day forward: Before one stone was placed on another in the temple of the LORD,

units.leftText: Through all that time, when one came to a heap of twenty measures, there were only ten. When one came to the wine vat to draw out fifty, there were only twenty.
units.rightText: from that time, when one came expecting a heap of twenty ephahs of grain, there were but ten. When one came to the winepress to draw out fifty baths, there were but twenty.
rightNotes: 2:16 Literally to draw out fifty from the winepress

units.leftText: I struck you with blight, mildew, and hail in all the work of your hands; yet you didn’t turn to me,’ says the LORD.
units.rightText: I struck you— all the work of your hands— with blight, mildew, and hail, but you did not turn to Me, declares the LORD.

units.leftText: ‘Consider, please, from this day and backward, from the twenty-fourth day of the ninth month, since the day that the foundation of the LORD’s temple was laid, consider it.
units.rightText: Consider carefully from this day forward — from the twenty-fourth day of the ninth month, the day the foundation of the LORD’s temple was laid — consider carefully:

units.leftText: Is the seed yet in the barn? Yes, the vine, the fig tree, the pomegranate, and the olive tree haven’t produced. From today I will bless you.’”
units.rightText: Is there still seed in the barn? The vine, the fig, the pomegranate, and the olive tree have not yet yielded fruit. But from this day on, I will bless you.” Zerubbabel the LORD’s Signet Ring

units.leftText: The LORD’s word came the second time to Haggai in the twenty-fourth day of the month, saying,
units.rightText: For the second time that day, the twenty-fourth day of the month, the word of the LORD came to Haggai, saying,

units.leftText: “Speak to Zerubbabel, governor of Judah, saying, ‘I will shake the heavens and the earth.
units.rightText: “Tell Zerubbabel governor of Judah that I am about to shake the heavens and the earth:

units.leftText: I will overthrow the throne of kingdoms. I will destroy the strength of the kingdoms of the nations. I will overthrow the chariots and those who ride in them. The horses and their riders will come down, everyone by the sword of his brother.
units.rightText: I will overturn royal thrones and destroy the power of the kingdoms of the nations. I will overturn chariots and their riders; horses and their riders will fall, each by the sword of his brother.

units.leftText: In that day, says the LORD of Armies, I will take you, Zerubbabel my servant, the son of Shealtiel,’ says the LORD, ‘and will make you like a signet ring, for I have chosen you,’ says the LORD of Armies.”
units.rightText: On that day, declares the LORD of Hosts, I will take you, My servant, Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel, declares the LORD, and I will make you like My signet ring, for I have chosen you, declares the LORD of Hosts.”
